new.title: Walk the walls of Çeşme Castle
new.desc: Genoese-origin fortress at the harbour, rebuilt by Sultan Bayezid II in 1508 and later extended. Its rooms hold the Çeşme Museum with finds from Ildırı and local history.
new.tip: Open daily except Mondays; climb to the ramparts for views of the harbour. Entry fee is small.
new.q: Çeşme Kalesi, Cumhuriyet Meydanı, Çeşme, İzmir

new.title: See the 1528 Çeşme Caravanserai
new.desc: Built on the orders of Süleyman the Magnificent beside the castle to house foreign merchants. It now operates as a hotel but the courtyard and arcades are worth a look.
new.tip: The courtyard cafe is open to non-guests; go in the evening when it is lit.

new.title: Visit Ayios Haralambos Church
new.desc: Greek Orthodox church built in 1832 and restored by Çeşme Municipality in 2012. It now hosts exhibitions and cultural events and is free to enter.
new.tip: Check the municipality programme for current exhibitions.

new.title: Meet Gazi Hasan Pasha and his lion at the harbour
new.desc: The statue of Cezayirli Gazi Hasan Pasha, the Ottoman admiral, stands in the main square beside the harbour with his pet lion. The square is the centre of the old town.
new.tip: Best at sunset, with the castle behind you.
new.q: Cezayirli Gazi Hasan Paşa Heykeli, Çeşme Meydanı, Çeşme, İzmir

new.title: Climb up to the Alaçatı windmills
new.desc: Stone windmills from around the 1850s stand on the ridge above Alaçatı, once grinding the village grain. Several have been restored as cafes and shops.
new.tip: Free to visit any time; sunset is best.
new.q: Alaçatı Yel Değirmenleri, Alaçatı, Çeşme, İzmir

new.title: Stroll Hacı Memiş Street in Alaçatı
new.desc: The cobbled lanes of Hacı Memiş and Kemalpaşa streets are lined with 19th-century Greek stone houses with bright shutters, now boutiques, wine bars and restaurants.
new.tip: Visit mid-morning on weekdays; evenings and weekends are very crowded.
new.q: Hacı Memiş Caddesi, Alaçatı, Çeşme, İzmir

new.title: Wander Alaçatı back lanes of stone houses
new.desc: Beyond the main streets are quiet lanes of restored Rum houses with bougainvillea and carved doors. The village was largely Greek until the 1923 population exchange.
new.tip: Start near the Alaçatı bazaar square and head east.

new.title: See the 6th-century BC Klazomenai olive oil workshop
new.desc: Restored workshop with pressing platforms and pits at the ancient city of Klazomenai, among the oldest known olive oil installations in the Aegean. It was reconstructed in situ and is open to visitors.
new.tip: Combine with Limantepe nearby; bring water, there is little shade.
new.q: Klazomenai Zeytinyağı Atölyesi, Urla İskele, Urla, İzmir

new.title: Explore Limantepe, the prehistoric mound of Klazomenai
new.desc: Excavations at Limantepe near Urla İskele have revealed Bronze Age fortifications and one of the earliest harbours of the Ionian coast. Panels explain the site.
new.tip: Open-air site; go in spring or autumn.
new.q: Limantepe Höyüğü, Urla İskele, Urla, İzmir

new.title: Browse Urla Art Street
new.desc: A pedestrianised street of restored stone houses in central Urla with galleries, craft shops and cafes. It is the heart of the town revived cultural scene.
new.tip: Visit Thursday to Sunday afternoons when most workshops are open.
new.q: Urla Sanat Sokağı, İskele Caddesi, Urla, İzmir

new.title: See the 16th-century Hızır Bey Mosque in Urla
new.desc: Ottoman mosque in the centre of Urla built in the 16th century and one of the oldest in the area. Its stonework fits the surrounding old market district.
new.tip: Dress modestly; outside prayer times only.

new.title: Spot Karantina Island off Urla İskele
new.desc: A small island in the bay used as a quarantine station in Ottoman and early Republican times, with old buildings still standing. It is a landmark of the Urla İskele waterfront.
new.tip: View it from the pier; boat rides run from İskele in summer.
new.q: Karantina Adası, Urla İskele, Urla, İzmir

new.title: Watch the fishing boats at Dalyan
new.desc: Quiet fishing village on the north coast of Çeşme with a small harbour and seafront fish restaurants, away from the resort strip. Tied to the old fishing economy of the town.
new.tip: Come at sunset for views toward Chios.
new.q: Dalyan Balıkçı Barınağı, Dalyan, Çeşme, İzmir

new.title: Visit the old stone village of Germiyan
new.desc: Small village of traditional stone houses and olive groves in the interior of Çeşme, little changed by tourism. It is a quiet counterpoint to the coast.
new.tip: Drive; take care on narrow lanes, and be back before dark.

new.title: Look over Gülbahçe Bay and its olive hills
new.desc: Quiet bay near Urla known for its olive groves, small marina and views across the Gulf of İzmir. It is home to the İzmir Institute of Technology campus.
new.tip: Quiet on weekdays; good for a drive.

new.title: See the olive groves at Zeytinalanı
new.desc: Seaside village between Urla and Çeşmealtı surrounded by old olive trees running to the water. Part of the olive oil heritage of Urla.
new.tip: Spring and autumn are the best for walking.

new.title: Book the tasting menu at OD Urla
new.desc: Hilltop estate restaurant opened in 2018 among vineyards, with a glasshouse and terrace. Its menu is built around Aegean produce and estate wine and has earned a Michelin star.
new.tip: Reserve well in advance; dinner is the main service.
new.q: OD Urla, Zeytinler Mah., Urla, İzmir

new.title: Dine at Teruar Urla among the vines
new.desc: Tasting-menu restaurant within a seven-room boutique hotel set among vineyards and olive trees. The kitchen focuses on terroir-driven Aegean cooking.
new.tip: Book ahead and ask for the wine pairing.

new.title: Try the seasonal set menu at Vino Locale
new.desc: Chef Ozan Kumbasar runs a small eight-table restaurant in Urla with a seasonal set menu that changes every six weeks and local wines.
new.tip: Reservations essential; ask about the vegetarian menu.

new.title: Taste village cooking at Osman Sezener
new.desc: Urla restaurant noted by food writers for its local produce and its place in the farm-to-table scene of the area.
new.tip: Check opening days before going.

new.title: Taste wines at Urla Şarapçılık
new.desc: One of the cornerstone wineries of the Urla Wine Route, with a tasting room and a restaurant overlooking the vineyards.
new.tip: Book a tasting in advance in busy months.

new.title: Taste Syrah and local wines at USCA
new.desc: Founding member of the Urla Wine Route with vineyards around Urla and a tasting room open to visitors.
new.tip: Call ahead to book a tasting.

new.title: Sip wine at Mozaik Vineyard in Urla
new.desc: Small Urla wine estate on the wine route offering tastings among its vineyards. Details on opening should be confirmed before going.
new.tip: Book a tasting in advance.

new.title: Visit Kaya Vineyard for a tasting near Urla
new.desc: Winery in the Urla area with vineyards and a tasting room. Confirm visiting hours as it works mostly by appointment.
new.tip: Phone ahead.

new.title: Taste at Çakır Şarapçılık, newest on the route
new.desc: Winery described as the newest addition to the Urla Wine Route, with its first bottling in 2018.
new.tip: Book tastings ahead.

new.title: Stop at the small cellar of Urlice
new.desc: Small, rustic winery and founding member of the Urla Wine Route, with simple tastings.
new.tip: Bring cash and call first.

new.title: Dinner at Asma Yaprağı in Alaçatı
new.desc: One of the best-known restaurants of Alaçatı, serving Aegean and Turkish dishes in a garden in the old town.
new.tip: Book on summer weekends; try the herb dishes.

new.title: Have a Turkish breakfast at Yer Fıstığı
new.desc: Alaçatı cafe recommended for a traditional Turkish breakfast spread with local cheeses, olives and jams.
new.tip: Arrive before 11 on weekends.
new.q: Yer Fıstığı Kahvaltı & Cafe, Alaçatı, Çeşme, İzmir

new.title: Eat a kumru sandwich at Kumrucu Şevki
new.desc: Çeşme is known for kumru, a toasted roll filled with sucuk, cheese and tomato. Kumrucu Şevki is a popular kumru stop.
new.tip: Order it with a glass of ayran.

new.title: Grab an Ilıca kumru by the beach
new.desc: The seafront cafes of Ilıca serve the signature kumru of Çeşme, a crisp roll with sucuk and cheese.
new.tip: Best after a swim; busy at lunchtime.

new.title: Try mastic puddings at an Alaçatı muhallebici
new.desc: Milk-pudding shops in Alaçatı serve desserts flavoured with mastic (sakız), a resin grown on nearby Chios and used across the peninsula.
new.tip: Try the sakızlı muhallebi.

new.title: Taste mastic ice cream in Çeşme
new.desc: Dondurma flavoured with mastic is a local speciality sold at ice-cream parlours near the harbour.
new.tip: Eat it near the castle.

new.title: Have a seafood lunch on the Urla İskele waterfront
new.desc: Urla İskele has a line of fish restaurants facing the bay, a long-standing weekend outing from İzmir.
new.tip: Fish is priced by weight; check before ordering.
new.q: Urla İskele Balıkçılar, Urla İskele, Urla, İzmir

new.title: Order the artichoke dishes in Urla
new.desc: Urla is known across İzmir for its spring artichokes, served in olive-oil dishes in local restaurants.
new.tip: Season runs roughly March to May.

new.title: Learn windsurfing in Alaçatı Bay
new.desc: Alaçatı Bay has shallow water and steady summer winds and is one of the windsurfing centres of Europe, with several schools along the beach.
new.tip: The afternoon wind is strongest; beginners go in the morning.
new.q: Alaçatı Surf Paradise, Alaçatı, Çeşme, İzmir

new.title: Take a kitesurf lesson on Alaçatı Bay
new.desc: Schools at Alaçatı offer IKO-certified lessons in the flat bay. It is regarded as a good beginner kite beach.
new.tip: Check the wind forecast the day before.
new.q: Kitesurf Alaçatı Bay, Alaçatı, Çeşme, İzmir

new.title: Browse the Saturday market in Alaçatı
new.desc: Weekly market drawing locals and day visitors with produce, cheeses, herbs and crafts, about 3 km from Çeşme.
new.tip: Go early before the crowds and heat.

new.title: Join the Alaçatı Herb Festival
new.desc: Four-day spring festival begun in 2010 celebrating the wild greens of the Aegean, with food stalls, tastings and workshops in the old town.
new.tip: Held around early April; book rooms ahead.
new.q: Alaçatı Ot Festivali, Alaçatı, Çeşme, İzmir

new.title: Swim at Ilıca Beach
new.desc: Shallow, family-friendly beach of about 2 km where thermal springs warm the water, one of the best-known beaches of the peninsula.
new.tip: Weekday mornings are calmer.

new.title: Soak in the thermal springs at Şifne
new.desc: Şifne is one of the two best-known hot-spring areas of the peninsula, with thermal pools and spa hotels.
new.tip: Many baths are in hotels; call for day passes.

new.title: Swim at Altınkum Beach
new.desc: Golden sand beach near central Çeşme facing open water, so the sea is cooler and livelier.
new.tip: Bring shade; facilities are limited.

new.title: Spend a day at Ayayorgi Bay
new.desc: Cove with beach clubs and a social atmosphere on the west coast of the peninsula.
new.tip: Arrive early for sunbeds in July and August.

new.title: Surf or swim at Pırlanta Beach
new.desc: Pırlanta (Diamond Beach) at Çiftlikköy is known for windsurfing and kitesurfing, with equipment rental and lessons.
new.tip: Wind picks up after midday.

new.title: Swim in the calm waters at Boyalık
new.desc: Quiet beach between Ilıca and Çeşme with calm, pool-like water on windless days.
new.tip: Lunch at the beach cafes.

new.title: Take a dip at Dalyan beach
new.desc: Small beach at the entrance to Dalyan, easy to reach from central Çeşme.
new.tip: Good for an evening swim.

new.title: Cycle the Urla wine and olive roads
new.desc: Gently rolling lanes link the wineries and olive groves of Urla Bağlarası, popular with cyclists.
new.tip: Spring and autumn; carry water.

new.title: Shop the Thursday bazaar in Ilıca
new.desc: Local market in Ilıca selling fresh fruit, vegetables and fish.
new.tip: Go early for the best fish.

new.title: Go sailing or SUP from Alaçatı Marina
new.desc: Alaçatı Port offers boat trips, rentals and watersports around the bay.
new.tip: Check the wind before booking.
new.q: Alaçatı Port Marina, Alaçatı, Çeşme, İzmir

new.title: Swim at Ovacık beach
new.desc: Rocky and sandy coves west of Çeşme with clear water.
new.tip: Wear water shoes on the rocks.

new.title: Swim at Çeşmealtı near Urla
new.desc: Seaside resort at the start of the Karaburun road on the south coast of Urla, with small beaches and fish restaurants.
new.tip: Quieter than Çeşme in July.

new.title: Take a boat trip from Çeşme harbour
new.desc: Day boats leave the harbour for swim stops in the bays around the peninsula, a classic Çeşme summer outing.
new.tip: Book at the harbour kiosks; choose a morning departure.
